Commentary.Commentary: We are back for India's reply.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, West Indies will be the happier of the two sides at the halfway mark. Moreover, they have the resources to defend this total. Considering the variable bounce off the surface, the chase isn't going to be easy for India and they will need to bat smartly to get over the line. Can the Indian batters rise to the occasion? We shall find out. Back in a bit for the chase...

Brandon King is in for a chat. He says that in the first 6 overs, they talked about getting to 150 and they are happy with it. Adds that personally, he found it a bit difficult to get going due to uneven bounce and to play spin on this track is challenging. Says that they have shown in the last two games that they can bowl well and is confident of getting the job done.

On the other hand, India will be a bit disheartened with how things went in the penultimate over. At the start, Hardik Pandya opted to introduce Yuzvendra Chahal and Axar Patel inside the Powerplay and this plan seemed to have backfired as both spinners were taken on by the West Indies openers. This move eventually paid off as Axar Patel got rid of Kyler Mayers. Returning to the side for this game, Kuldeep Yadav worked his magic and struck thrice in the middle overs to pile misery on the West Indies. With two relatively new batters at the crease, India would have fancied themselves to keep them quiet. However, it did not go as they would have liked towards the back end of the innings. Kuldeep Yadav was the pick of the bowlers for India with figures of 3 for 28 in his four overs.

Mukesh Kumar nailed his yorkers in the final over but Rovman Powell's late flourish has helped West Indies post 159 on the board! After Rovman Powell won the toss and opted to bat, the opening pair of Brandon King and Kyle Mayers were circumspect in the first couple of overs but took on the Indian spinners who were introduced inside the Powerplay. With a solid 55-run opening stand, they laid a solid foundation for the West Indies innings. Nicholas Pooran continued where he left off in the previous game and looked set for another valuable knock but his stay was cut short by Kuldeep Yadav. With wickets falling at the other end, Bradon King's momentum was hampered and he followed Pooran back into the hut soon after. At that stage, the West Indies needed someone to put their hands and so did their skipper, Rovman Powell. His unbeaten cameo of 40 runs off just 19 balls has propelled his side to 159.

Well bowled but they do get the brace. Mukesh Kumar nails the yorker on middle and leg, Rovman Powell stays deep again and jams it out in front of mid-wicket. The batters push hard and get back for two eventually. West Indies finish with 159/5 on the board!

Commentary.Commentary: Take two and now we are all set for the game to begin. Umpires out in the middle and the fielders are in place. It will be the pair of Kyle Mayers and Brandon King to open the innings for West Indies. Hardik Pandya, the Indian skipper has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

We are all set! The two umpires are out in the middle and so are the players of India. There is a slight delay though because the groundstaff have forgotten to mark the inner circle. The players and the umpires go back into the hut as the groundstaff start their work. Stay tuned as this won't be a long delay.

PITCH REPORT - Ian Bishop is near the pitch and Daren Ganga joins him in the middle. Ganga says that the surface is drier than the one used in the 2nd game and it is a bit dusty but there will be consistent bounce. Reckons the spinners will come into the game more.

Hardik Pandya, the skipper of India, says that they don't mind chasing. Adds that they would have preferred to bat first. Reckons that the surface might get slower. Mentions that Nicholas Pooran has been batting well and says that they want to keep things simple against him. Informs that Yashasvi Jaiswal makes his T20 debut, replacing Ishan Kishan and Ravi Bishnoi makes way for Kuldeep Yadav.

Rovman Powell, the West Indies skipper says that they will bat first as the wicket looks a bit slow, and wants to put runs on the board. Informs that Jason Holder picked up a niggle in the knee in the last game and hence, he is rested and Roston Chase comes in for him. Mentions that the boys are excited and a series win will be good for not just the team but for the board and the fans as well. Says that against a strong side like India, you need to always press and not get too predictable.

India (Playing XI) - Shubman Gill, Yashasvi Jaiswal (In for Ishan Kishan), Suryakumar Yadav, Tilak Varma, Hardik Pandya (C), Sanju Samson (WK), Axar Patel, Kuldeep Yadav (In for Ravi Bishnoi), Arshdeep Singh, Yuzvendra Chahal, Mukesh Kumar.

West Indies (Playing XI) - Brandon King, Kyle Mayers, Johnson Charles, Nicholas Pooran (WK), Rovman Powell (C), Shimron Hetmyer, Romario Shepherd, Roston Chase (In for Jason Holder), Akeal Hosein, Alzarri Joseph, Obed McCoy.
TOSS - The two captains are out in the middle. The coin toss lands in the favour of Rovman Powell and the West Indies have opted to BAT first.

Debut Alert - Left-handed batter Yashasvi Jaiswal has been handed his maiden T20I cap and is all set to make his T20I debut for India. He had made his Test debut earlier in the tour and will now represent India in the T20I format. It was a dream international debut for the young man, can he replicate the same here? Also, who is going to make way for him? Stay tuned to find out...

On the other hand, India's lacklustre batting has resulted in them losing the first two T20Is of this five-match T20I series. Tilak Varma has been one of the positives for them, but the rest of the batting group will need to stand up in what is a must-win game for them. The bowlers have done their job in both games and will have to do even better against the in-form West Indies batters. Will Hardik Pandya's men manage to keep the series alive? Or will we see the West Indies seal the series with yet another win? Plenty of answers to unfold, so stick around as the toss and team news is coming up in a bit.

Having come from behind to pull off an unlikely victory in the first T20I, the West Indies turned up to Guyana with momentum behind them to make it 2-0. The hosts were up to the mark with their discipline with the ball and kept India in check. In their pursuit of a tricky total, they stuttered a bit, but Nicholas Pooran and the tail came to the rescue and took them over the line. History beckons for Rovman Powell and Co., who have never clinched a bilateral T20I series against India consisting of 3 or more games.

Hello and a warm welcome, ladies and gentlemen, to our coverage of the third T20I between the West Indies and India at the Providence Stadium in Guyana. We have had two thrillers so far, and this one promises to be even more exciting with the series on the line for India. On the other hand, the West Indies are riding high on confidence and will want to seal the series in this game itself before the two teams make the trip to Lauderhill in the USA for the last two T20Is.
... MATCH DAY ...

We are now down to the third T20I of the five-match T20I series between the West Indies and India, which will take place at the Providence Stadium in Guyana. After a stunning victory in the first T20I at Tarouba, West Indies turned up at Guyana as well to take a 2-0 lead in the series. Rovman Powell and Co. now find themselves on the cusp of a series win against the top-ranked T20I side, India. In the second T20I, after Hardik Pandya called it right and opted to bat first, India kept losing wickets at regular intervals in their batting effort. Tilak Varma continued where he left off on his T20I debut and stroked his maiden T20I fifty to keep the visitors afloat. With the ball, India were off to a dream start courtesy of Hardik Pandya's twin strikes in the first over. Nicholas Pooran continued his brilliant form in the format and brought up his second consecutive T20I fifty to keep his side in a commanding position. However, his dismissal triggered a collapse that put the West Indies on the brink of a loss. But Akeal Hosein and Alzarri Joseph held their nerves and took their side over the line with seven balls to spare. India's batters have let them down in the first two T20Is, and as they look to keep the series alive, the likes of Ishan Kishan, Suryakumar Yadav, and Tilak Varma will have to click together. Shubman Gill isn't having the best of the series, scoring just 10 runs in the two T20Is, and might have to make way for Yashasvi Jaiswal. Moreover, India's long tail has made matters worse for them, in which case both Gill and Jaiswal might feature at the expense of one of the three spinners. Kuldeep Yadav missed the second T20I due to a sore left thumb, and his return will make a huge difference for the visitors. On the other hand, the West Indian top order has failed to deliver as per expectations so far. That said, Nicholas Pooran and Rovman Powell have been consistent, which has made the job easier for the rest of the batting unit. In the second T20I, Jason Holder walked back into the shed with a hamstring strain, and his availability in the remaining three T20Is will depend on the extent of the injury. The first two T20Is have been thrilling contests, and the third T20I promises to be no exception. Will the West Indies manage to gain an unassailable 3-0 lead in the series? Or will we see India hit back and keep the series alive? We will find out together.
